one_month_reasoning: Q3 2026 results are listed by MarketBeat/TipRanks for Nov 3, 2026 (before the open), i.e. just after the Oct 30 window. That date is not confirmed by an Eaton release I could reach (the Eaton IR page returned 503), and Q2 was reported on July 31, so there is some chance (~25%) the release lands inside the window. Company Q3 guide is adj EPS $3.46-3.56, organic growth 13.5-15.5%, segment margin 24.6-25.0%. The Laguna conference (Sep 16) already signalled strength: data-center orders +85%, pricing moving to a tailwind. That leaves little room for a guide-driven surprise before the print. Other items in the window are hyperscaler Q3 capex commentary in late October (read-across for data-center demand, direction ?) and routine Dana/RMT filings (neutral). The stock rose ~8% in the week after Laguna and closed at $432, below the $478 high, so I see no strong momentum or reversal signal. I centred the distribution on today's price with a small positive drift (~0.4%) and monthly vol of 39%/3.5 ≈ 11%, lognormal, taking no directional view.

fair_value.method: Blend of forward P/E (65%): NTM EPS at Sep-2027 of ~$17.3 x 26x = $450; and FCF yield (35%): NTM FCF ~$5.1B ex-Mobility / ~382M shares = $13.4/share at a 3.0% yield = $445. Blended ≈ $448.

inputs_detail.derivation: Consensus is ~$15.64-15.80 (src 9). I take 2027 as +15.5% on the $13.50 2026 midpoint. Support: EA backlog +33%, Electrical Global backlog +103%, Aero +28% (src 1, 4); management says price/cost turns into a 2027 tailwind (src 5). Offset: I cut ~$0.2 for net RMT dilution. Mobility ran ~$109M/qtr of operating profit (src 1), is valued at ~$5.1B (src 3) and is swapped for retired ETN shares plus $1.1B of cash (src 2).
+15% growth. The Q2 call says ~80% of the 307 GW US data-center backlog converts in 2028 and beyond (src 6). Management keeps a 32% EA margin target by 2030 (src 6).

The stock trades at ~27.7x 2027 consensus ($432/$15.7, src 9, 10) and ~32x 2026 guidance (src 1). I assume the multiple de-rates about 1.5 turns as growth normalises from 12% organic toward the high single digits and teens. Premium versus the ~20x electrical-equipment history is kept because of the backlog visibility.

methods.name: FCF yield
methods.inputs: NTM FCF at Sep-2027 ~$5.1B ex-Mobility; diluted shares ~382M after split-off; 3.0% FCF yield

inputs_detail.derivation: FY26 ~$4.0B (H1 $1.19B + seasonally strong H2, as in Q4'25's $1.6B). FCF then grows ~20%/yr with EPS and Boyd, less ~$0.35B of Mobility FCF.

389.5M diluted (src 1). About 7-9M shares are retired in the exchange offer: Eaton holders' ≥50.1% stake in a ~$10B+ combined company is worth ~$3-4B at $432 per ETN share (src 2, 3). No buybacks in H1 2026 (src 4).

Current FY26E FCF of ~$4.0B on a ~$168B market cap is ~2.4%. I apply a modestly higher 3.0% yield on NTM cash flow, consistent with the P/E de-rating assumption. Net debt is ~$19.9B after the Boyd/Ultra PCS deals (src 1, 4) and is partly paid down with the $1.1B RMT cash.

bear.story: Hyperscaler capex digestion or financing stress slows data-center orders in 2027. EA margin recovery to the 30s stalls. Boyd integration and the $19.9B net debt weigh. 2027 EPS is ~$14.5 and the multiple compresses to ~20x NTM.

base.story: Backlog converts and price turns into a tailwind. The RMT closes in Q1 2027. EPS is $15.6 in 2027 and ~$17.9 in 2028, and the multiple de-rates slightly to ~26x NTM EPS.

bull.story: Data-center orders keep compounding (negotiation pipeline +130%), 800V DC and solid-state transformer wins arrive, and EA margin heads toward 32% early. 2028 EPS is ~$19 and the stock holds ~31x as a grid-to-chip leader.

thesis_break_reason: At $330 the stock would sit at ~21x 2027 consensus EPS, near the $312 52-week low. The market would be pricing a genuine break in the data-center order cycle (orders or backlog cancellations) or a failure of the promised 450-500bp H2 EA margin recovery, not ordinary 39%-vol noise. A negative 12-month rolling order print in Electrical Americas would confirm it.

key_uncertainties: Durability of hyperscaler/AI data-center capex into 2027-28. Data-center revenue is up ~65% and orders ~85%, so this is the dominant driver.
Pace of EA margin recovery. Segment margin guidance was cut from 24.6-25.0% to 24.1-24.5% even as the EPS guide rose, due to price/cost and capacity-ramp costs.
Multiple compression risk from ~28x forward as growth rates peak.
Leverage after $13B of acquisitions (net debt ~$19.9B, $2.1B commercial paper).
RMT execution: timing, exchange ratio, and the final share retirement versus EPS dilution.
reasoning: Primary documents drive the view. The Q2 release and 10-Q show 14% organic growth, record $8.5B sales, and backlogs up 33% in EA, 103% in EG (Boyd) and 28% in Aero, with $24.1B total firm backlog. The FY26 adjusted EPS guide was raised to $13.40-13.60, but the segment margin guide was quietly lowered by 50bp versus the January guide, which is a detail recaps skip. No buybacks were made in H1, and debt jumped to ~$20.6B after Boyd ($9.55B) and Ultra PCS ($1.53B). The Mobility RMT with Dana is a split-off: ETN holders exchange shares, and Eaton receives $1.1B cash. It is roughly value-neutral per share and slightly EPS-dilutive, and closes in Q1 2027. At the Sep 16 Laguna conference management said price/cost flips to a tailwind in 2027, data-center orders are +85%, and the pipeline is +130%. They also flagged a 'more measured' capacity ramp and bolt-on-only M&A. Valuation is P/E at 26x NTM EPS of $17.3 = $450, and FCF yield at 3% on $13.4/share = $445, blending to a fair value of ~$448. That is ~4% above spot and close to the ~$456-464 consensus target (used as evidence only). Scenarios are $300/$455/$590 at 22/53/25%. The ladder is a lognormal with median ~$448 and ~35% vol, a bit below the 39% realized because the base rate for large caps is 25-35% and backlog visibility is high. The left tail is fattened slightly for an AI-capex air pocket. Research limits: Alpha Vantage was rate-limited, the Twelve Data estimate endpoints were paywalled, and the Eaton IR events page and the COL Group release were unreachable. The consensus EPS comes from aggregator pages.
